title: The Same Crossing
logline: A ferryman makes the same short lagoon crossing dozens of times a day, in flat dawn stillness and in a wind-driven afternoon chop, arriving each time at the same far bank by a different road.
human_question: If two people reach the same place, does it matter that they got there so differently?

premise.story: A day and a season with a lagoon or river ferry operator, following the same short crossing in very different water and weather.
premise.place: A lagoon or river ferry crossing.
premise.experience: Repetition with variation: the same short journey made calm and made hard, arriving at an identical point each time.

concept_links.why: The source counts the moment of path and fruition again by the depth of absorption behind it: the destination is the same, but the texture of arrival differs, glad at four levels, evenly calm at the deepest [C017-P:L25; C017-M:L3–L11]. The ferry's identical crossing in different water is an honest, loose echo of a journey's texture changing while its endpoint does not.
The source's own word for these minds rests on the image of 'carrying across' to the far side [C016-P:L25].

what_camera_could_observe: The same crossing at dawn stillness and in a rough afternoon current
Passengers' reasons for crossing, ordinary and varied
The ferryman's reading of the water, his adjustments
The moment of arrival, similar each time despite very different journeys
what_must_be_real: A real, working ferry crossing and its actual operator and passengers. Weather is not engineered; the film follows what the season brings.

possible_arc.turn: The same crossing attempted in rough water.
possible_arc.ending_open: The ferryman's own account of the difference, if he chooses to give one.

requirements: A working ferry crossing with a willing operator
Filming across enough of a season to capture different water conditions
Passenger consent for any close filming
